title: Asiya in Pharaoh's house
hook: Pharaoh's wife, who kept faith in the harshest house (66:11)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Maryam, and your line: named. Did you say a woman's name out loud, and what she did? Today, a woman the Qur'an never names, and sets beside Maryam anyway. Day six hundred seventy-two, the end of a week.

Think of the worst possible address for a person of faith. Not a desert, not a prison. A palace. The palace of the man who declared himself lord most high, who had the baby boys of a whole people killed. And inside it, married to him, a woman who believed. The Qur'an calls her only the wife of Pharaoh. Tradition gives her the name Asiya. She first appears on a riverbank, looking at a basket.

Surah al-Qasas tells it. Pharaoh's household pulls a baby out of the river, the baby Musa. In a house that kills boys, his wife speaks first: he'll be a comfort of the eye for me and for you, don't kill him; maybe he'll be useful to us, or we'll take him as a son. Her first recorded words save a prophet's life. Years later, in surah sixty-six, she speaks again, and this time it's a prayer. In Pickthall's translation: "My Lord! Build for me a home with Thee in the Garden." She goes on to ask to be saved from Pharaoh and his deeds, and from a wrongdoing people. The Qur'an sets her up as an example for all believers, and in the next verse sets Maryam beside her. Two women, one in a palace and one under a palm. Notice the order of her words in Arabic: rabbi-bni li 'indaka baytan fil-jannah. 'Indaka, with You, comes before baytan, a house. Scholars love that detail: she asked for the neighbor before the house. What happened to her, the Qur'an doesn't say. Commentators tell stories of her suffering for her faith; those come from later reports, not from the verse. What the hadith does say, in al-Bukhari, is that many men reached perfection, but among women only Maryam and Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh. She didn't leave the house. She couldn't. She kept her faith inside it, and saved a child while she was there.

The practice: keep faith in a hard place. Sit, and think of the place in your life that's hardest to be good in. A job, a family table, a group chat, a relationship. Somewhere you can't simply walk out of. Picture yourself there. Now ask: what's one small thing I could protect in that place, the way Asiya protected a baby? A kind word, a boundary, a quiet prayer, someone weaker than me. If you pray, you can say her line: my Lord, build for me a home with You. The bell holds the time.
Asiya in Pharaoh's house. Pharaoh's believing wife, who saved the baby Musa and prayed for a home with Allah, with You before the house. Today's word.

Your line: faith in pharaoh's house. This week went from faith in the unseen, a healing, seek knowledge, the world is signs and water is mercy, to named. Today, in your hardest place, protect one small good thing. Day six hundred seventy-two.

howItsDone: Muslims honor Asiya as one of the most perfect women, alongside Maryam; her prayer in 66:11 is often recited, especially by people enduring hardship.
